'''Turi''' is an endangered [[Austroasiatic language]] of India that belongs to the [[Munda languages|Kherwarian Munda]] group.{{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|p=262}} Grierson (1906) described that Turi is similar to both [[Mundari language|Mundari]] and [[Santali language|Santali]]. It is spoken by only half a percent of ethnic Turi, the rest having shifted to [[Sadri language|Sadri]] in Jharkhand, Mundari in West Bengal, and [[Odia language|Odia]] in [[Odisha]]. The Turi are classified as a [[Scheduled Caste]] in Jharkhand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.censusindia.gov.in/2011census/PCA/SC.html|title=Census of India|publisher=Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India|website=www.censusindia.gov.in|access-date=2018-07-26}}</ref>

==Classification==
Turi has been traditionally grouped with the Mundaric dialect continuum. A recent phylogenetic analysis on Turi conducted by Peterson, et al. (2024) using the software COG from the [[Summer Institute of Linguistics]] found that Turi forms a closer cline with the [[Santali language|Santali]] dialect continuum rather than with the Mundari-[[Ho language|Ho]] dialects. This result is more aligned with the classification of Turi proposed by ''[[Ethnologue]]'' (Eberhard et al. (2023)). The analysis concludes that Turi may have separated from the Kherwarian languages groups from an early date so that it may constitute a third subgroup of Kherwarian.{{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|p=286}}

==Phonology==
===Consonants===
Similar to Santali and Mundari, but /w/ is replaced by /ʋ/ in Turi. Most Munda languages have voiced stops accompanied with pre-glottalization and nasal release, so does Turi, but the language tends to drop the stops entirely while retains the nasal and the glottal stop. Eg. Turi [uʔm] "hair", Mundari [uˀb̥ᵐ] "hair"; Turi [mɛʔn̪] "eye", Mundari [meˀd˺ⁿ] "eye".{{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|p=267}}

==Morphology==
===Nominals===
====Pronouns====
Emphasis on dual and plural reference in Turi pronouns can be reinforced by attaching number markers ''=kin'' and ''=ku'' directly to the pronoun. Eg. ''ɑliŋ bɑɾɑŋ=kin'' "we both (EXCL)", ''ɑlɛ=ku'' "we (PL.EXCL)".{{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|p=268}}

====Cases====
Turi has five cases. The case markers follow the number markers. For example, ''tʃɑʋɑ=kun=rɛn'' (child=PL=GEN) "of the children".{{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|pp=269-270}}

====Copulas====
Odisha Turi has two copulas: the temporary/locative ''hɛn='' (suppletive form ''kɑnɔʔɔ''){{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|p=275}} and identity ''=nɑŋ''. The origin of ''=nɑŋ'' is obscure.{{sfn|Peterson|Minz|Linda|Khan|2024|p=277}}
